g.text: Okafor's office wall is covered in paper: vendors, bank accounts, names, arrows. He wants it in a
spreadsheet by morning. "Eight invoices from Reyes's mailbox," he says. "Every field, every number, same
shape every time. If one amount comes back as a sentence, the chart is useless."
Bill to: Halcyon Maritime Logistics, Pier 9 Administration, Kestrel Bay
Remit to: Account 88-301-4471, Sabran Mercantile Bank
Here is the extracted invoice data in JSON format with the specified keys:

as a string, a made-up category.

"Total due as a plain number, no commas or currency"
"VAT registration, or null if none is printed"
Ollama turns the schema into a grammar. Tokens that would break it get zero probability.
. Check the machine against the paper

Valid JSON is not the same as correct JSON. The schema guarantees shape, not truth.
Categories need a human eye too: is a network switch
. Cross the Northwind rows with Malhotra's travel
Northwind invoices against R. Malhotra's approved travel
The join is ordinary Python. The model only had to produce rows a program can trust.
3 Northwind invoices, KBD 227,700.00 in total. None carries a VAT number. All of them remit to the same
account at Sabran Mercantile Bank. And every one is dated while Raj Malhotra was in Port Sabran on
Okafor pins a new card to the centre of his wall and draws three lines to it. "Operations does not
approve freight invoices," he says. "So why is every one of these coded to his cost centre?"
